BURHAN:v2p208/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p208/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p208/r5.claim: The word أمة is given with several senses across the Qur'an: a group, an exemplary leader, a religion, or a period of time.
BURHAN:v2p208/r5.anchor: وكالأمة فى قوله تعالى ﴿ وجد عليه أمة ﴾ بمعنى الجماعة وفي قوله ﴿ إن إبراهيم كان أمة ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p481/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r3.claim: Wajada can mean to encounter or come upon someone, as in the examples of the two women and the queen.
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r3.anchor: الخامس وجد بمعنى صادف قوله تعالى في سورة القصص ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان كقوله تعالى في سورة النحل إني وجدت امرأة تملكهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.claim: The Madyan episode displays virtues that prepared Moses for revelation: generosity, helping the distressed, compassion, modesty, gratitude, chastity, and fidelity; Shuaib likewise shows hospitality, protection of the fearful, and gentleness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.anchor: هو ما تضمنته من فضائل الأعمال ومناقب أهل الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.claim: These character traits could lead Meccan polytheists to compare Moses with Muhammad's known virtue before his mission and recognize the signs of revelation; Muslims should also emulate prophetic character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.anchor: ليعتبر المشركون بذلك إن كان لهم اعتبار في مقايسة تلك الأحوال بأجناسها من أحوال النبي

STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r7.claim: In Midian, Moses meets two sisters, marries one, and spends years working for his father-in-law.
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r7.anchor: There Moses meets two sisters, one of whom he will come to marry, and finds refuge for many years in the employ of his father-in-law

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r5.claim: مَاءَ can mean water or a well; the Torah calls it a well, and springs with narrow access are also difficult to use when crowded.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r5.anchor: may refer to water and also to a well

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r1.claim: Moses saw shepherds watering their flocks and two women holding their herd back; تَذُودَان indicates their animals pushed toward the water as the women pulled them back.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r1.anchor: their herd had reached the fountain and was pushing forward to drink water from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r2.claim: The women explained that their elderly father left them to tend the flock, and they waited until the male shepherds left because they could not force through the crowd.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r2.anchor: their father had grown very old and as a result

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r3.claim: The episode reflects distinct spheres for men and women: women did such work only under compulsion, carefully staying apart from men; the author criticizes reformers who advocate identical work spheres.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r3.anchor: they would do so, but only because of compulsion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r5.claim: Moses’ question مَا خَطْبُكُمَا asks about an important matter, conveying concern for the women’s difficult circumstances rather than casual curiosity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p534/r5.anchor: is used for some important matter

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.claim: Omitting a recoverable object can make speech more graceful; in وجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان, the omitted object is their camels, and poetry likewise leaves objects understood.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.anchor: أي: تذودان إبلهما، ولو نطق بالمفعول لما كان في عذوبة حذفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r5.claim: He reached the water of Midian; warada can mean reaching or entering, and the water was said to be a well. Umma is a large group, and عليه means at its bank or edge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r5.anchor: ولما ورد ماء مدين: أي وصل إليه، والورود بمعنى الوصول إلى الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the women kept their sheep from the water because they feared the stronger shepherds; Qatada says they kept people away from the sheep, and al-Zajjaj says they avoided crowding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r6.anchor: تذودان، قال ابن عباس وغيره: تذودان غنمهما عن الماء خوفا من السقاة الأقوياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes من دونهم to mean the women stood before the crowd relative to Moses; al-Zamakhshari says they were in a lower place than the shepherds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r1.claim: The women may have been shielding their faces from men's gaze; al-Farra says they restrained the flock from scattering and gives their names as Abra and Sabura.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r1.anchor: وقال الفراء: تحبسانها عن أن تتفرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says asking ما خطبكما is appropriate for someone afflicted, oppressed, needing compassion, or facing an unusual matter; al-Zamakhshari derives it from the object of a pursuit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والسؤال بالخطب إنما هو في مصاب، أو مضطهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r3.claim: Moses' question shows it is permissible to speak with an unrelated woman when a need arises; the sisters lacked a hired worker and waited for shepherds to finish, since they could not draw water or compete with men.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r3.anchor: وفي سؤاله عليه الصلاة والسلام دليل على جواز مكالمة الأجنبية فيما يعن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r4.speaker: شمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r4.claim: Shammar has a rare reading with kasra on خ, asking who their husband was and why he did not water for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ شمر: بكسر الخاء، أي من زوجكما؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r5.claim: Ibn Musarrif reads لا نسقي with damma on nun; readers vary whether the shepherds return with their flocks or drive the flocks back. The raʿaʾ readings vary, and al-Bahr rejects al-Zamakhshari's claim that its kasra plural is a regular pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مصرف: لا نسقي، بضم النون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r6.claim: Their father being an elderly man explains why they water the flock themselves and appeals to Moses for help.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296#2/r6.anchor: وأبونا شيخ كبير: اعتذار لموسى عن مباشرتهما السقي بأنفسهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p297/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p297/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p297/r3.claim: The women's answer fits Moses' question: they were weak and modest, unable to compete with men, and waited until shepherds left; their watering was permissible by Arab and Bedouin custom, especially under necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p297/r3.anchor: بأنا امرأتان ضعيفتان مستورتان، لا نقدر على مزاحمة الرجال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p121/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p121/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p121/r10.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr interprets ورود as presence or nearness, as when Moses arrived at the water of Midian; some choose this for everyone's coming near Hell and kneeling around it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p121/r10.anchor: وأخرج عبد ابن حميد عن عبيد بن عمير أن الورود الحضور والقرب كما في قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.claim: When echoing a noun with أي in a question, match its number and gender: رجل gives أيا, رجلين أَيَين, امرأة أية, امرأتين أيتين, and نسوة أيات.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.claim: The interrogative form follows the case of the noun in the preceding statement, because the question echoes the speaker's grammatical construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.anchor: على ما وضع عليه المتكلم كلامه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.claim: For a proper name, use من عبد الله rather than أيا; أي عبد الله is nominative and cannot echo case as من عبد الله can, because من is being used outside its usual construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكأنرجلالوقالرأيترجلاقلتأيافإ.anchor: إذا قال رأيت عبد الله قلت أي عبد الله

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r1.claim: تذودان describes the women, not a second object of وجد, which here means encountered.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r1.anchor: قوله: { تذودان }: صفة ل " امرأتين " لا مفعول ثان لأن " وجد " بمعنى لقي.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r2.claim: ذود means driving away or pushing back; an anonymous poetic line uses يذود for turning people away with a sword.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r3.claim: Another sense is holding back; the omitted object may be people from their flock or their flock from mingling with the crowd.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r3.anchor: وقيل: حبس، ومفعوله محذوف أي: تذودان الناس عن غنمهما، أو غنمهما عن مزاحمة الناس.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r4.claim: من دونهم means a place lower than the place occupied by the people watering.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r4.anchor: و " من دونهم " أي من مكان أسفل من مكانهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses the question as asking what they seek by holding the flock back; the sought object is called a خطب, like a concern is a شأن.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r5.anchor: وحقيقته ما مخطوبكما؟ أي: ما مطلوبكما من الذياد، سمى المخطوب خطبا، كما سمي المشؤون شأنا

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya says خطب is asked of someone afflicted or oppressed, someone eliciting concern, or someone doing something extraordinary.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " السؤال بالخطب إنما هو في مصاب أو مضطهد " أو من يشفق عليه، أو يأتي بمنكر من الأمر

SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r7.speaker: شمر
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r7.claim: Shammar's very anomalous kasra reading asks who their husbands are, or why neither the women nor their husbands are watering.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23/r7.anchor: وقرأ شمر " خطبكما " بالكسر أي: ما زوجكما؟ أي: لم تسقيان ولم يسق زوجكما؟ وهي شاذة جدا.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read يصدر intransitively from صدر: the herders return with their livestock.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر بفتح الياء وضم الدال من صدر يصدر وهو قاصر أي: يصدرون بمواشيهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r2.claim: Other readers use transitive أصدر; the omitted object is their livestock, which the herders send back.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r2.anchor: والباقون بضم الياء وكسر الدال مضارع أصدر معدى بالهمزة، والمفعول محذوف أي: يصدرون مواشيهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r3.claim: The common kasra in الرعاء is an irregular broken plural: a defective active participle such as قاض normally takes plural فعلة, as in قضاة and رماة.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r3.anchor: والعامة على كسر الراء من " الرعاء " وهو جمع تكسير غير مقيس؛ لأن فاعلا الوصف المعتل اللام كقاض قياسه فعلة نحو:

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analogizes kasra الرعاء to صيام and قيام, but the author says that analogy is mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وأما الرعاء بالكسر فقياس كصيام وقيام " وليس كما ذكر لما ذكرته.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r5.claim: In one transmission Abu Amr opens راء; Abu al-Fadl treats it as a verbal noun used adjectivally or an omitted construction. A damma reading is a collective noun.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية بفتح الراء. قال أبو الفضل: " هو مصدر أقيم مقام الصفة؛ فلذلك استوى فيه الواحد والجمع " ، أو على حذف مضاف.

SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r6.speaker: ابن مصرف
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r6.claim: Ibn Musarrif reads نسقي with damma on نون, from أسقى; the distinction between سقى and أسقى was discussed at al-Nahl.
SAMIN-DURR:28:23#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن مصرف " لا نسقي " بضم النون من أسقى، وقد تقدم الفرق بين سقى وأسقى في النحل.

ZAJJAJ:v4p139/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p139/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p139/r1.claim: Their aged father could not drive the flock away or water it, so the women had to do the watering.
ZAJJAJ:v4p139/r1.anchor: الفائدة في قوله: (وأبونا شيخ كبير). أي لا يمكنه أن يرد، ويسقي. فلذلك احتجنا ونحن نساء أن نسقي.

ASAD-NOTES:28:23#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:23#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:23#n21/r1.claim: The term in the phrase about reaching the wells of Madyan literally means "water" or "waters".

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read yaṣdura from the intransitive ṣadara, with an open yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر: (حتى يصدر) بنصب الياء ورفع الدال

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r2.claim: The others read yuṣdir from aʿṣdara, with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl; this means the shepherds bring their livestock away from the watering place.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: حتى يصدر برفع الياء وكسر الدال من أصدرت

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r3.claim: The phrase means until the shepherds return from watering; with the intransitive reading, they return, while the transitive reading omits the object, their flocks.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r3.anchor: [قال أبو علي] : (حتى يصدر الرعاء): حتى يرجعوا من سقيهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r4.claim: Omitting the object is common in the Qur'an and ordinary speech; the source compares لينذر بأسا شديدا, where the people being warned are omitted, and a poet's omitted أحدا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412#2/r4.anchor: فحذف المفعول، وحذف المفعول كثير في التنزيل وفي سائر الكلام

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r1.claim: With ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl, the verb is transitive: the shepherds bring their livestock away from the water.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم الياء أنه جعله فعلا هم فاعلوه يتعدى إلى مفعول

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r2.claim: With fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl, the verb is intransitive and describes the shepherds departing themselves.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح الياء أنه جعله فعلا لهم غير متعد إلى غيرهم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r3.claim: The imāla of ṣād toward zā brings it closer to the following dāl because ṣād is quiescent before it.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن أشم الصاد الزاي أنه قربها بذلك من الدال لسكون الصاد ومجيء الدال بعدها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r4.claim: الرعاء, with kasra on rāʾ and long vowel, is a plural of rāʿin; raʿūn is another sound plural and ruʿāt another broken plural.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r4.anchor: والرعاء بكسر الراء والمد جمع راع وفيه وجهان آخران راعون على السلامة ورعاة على التكسير

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r5.speaker: البصريون
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r5.claim: The Basrans derive رعاة from رعية, with yāʾ becoming alif because it is mobile and preceded by fatḥa.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r6.claim: The Kufans derive رعاة from رعى, deleting a letter to avoid doubling, adding hāʾ as compensation, and turning yāʾ into alif before hāʾ.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p276#2/r6.anchor: وأصله عند الكوفيين رعى فحذفوا حرفا كراهية للتشديد وألحقوا الهاء عوضا مما حذفوا

QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#1/r1.claim: Form I active yaṣdura means the shepherds themselves depart or issue forth, with the flocks implicit.
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#1/r1.anchor: Vr, mutawatir: "Form I active: ""until the shepherds (themselves) depart/issue forth"" — flocks implicit

QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#2/r1.speaker: ibdāl
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#2/r1.claim: This variant makes a minor phonetic assimilation of ṣād, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:28:23:25#2/r1.anchor: ibdāl, mutawatir: minor phonetic assimilation of the ṣād — no semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the two women were keeping people away from their sheep.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ تذودان ﴾ تذودان الناس عن غنمها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the women waited until the shepherds had departed, then drank the water they had left over.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ حتى يصدر الرعاء ﴾ قال فتشرب فضالتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r1.claim: Warada here means reached, not entered or drank; the water means the well from which people drew water, using the place for what occurs there.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r1.anchor: أي وصل اليه وورد والورود بمعنى الدخول وبمعنى الشرب وليس شيء منهما مرادا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r2.claim: ʿAlayhi means at the well's rim and watering place.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r3.claim: Umma denotes a large gathering of people of varied kinds; the indefinite form suggests abundance and min al-nās signals the different classes present.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r3.anchor: أي جماعة كثيرة مختلفي الأصناف ويشعر بالقيد الأول التنوين وبالثاني من الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r4.claim: Others take min al-nās to disparage the crowd as low people known only by their kind, or to clarify that they were human beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r4.anchor: وقيل فائدته تحقير أولئك الجماعة وأنهم لئام لا يعرفون بغير جنسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r5.claim: The people apparently watered different kinds of livestock; identifying their animals more narrowly would require transmitted evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r5.anchor: الظاهر أنهم كانوا يسقون مواشي مختلفة الأنواع بمعنى أن منهم من كان يسقي إبلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r6.claim: Min dūnihim may mean below their position; other explanations are nearby, apart from them, or on the side from which Moses first approached, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya says.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r6.anchor: أي في مكان أسفل من مكانهم وقيل : من قربهم أو من سواهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r7.claim: The daughters' names are variously given as Layā, ʿAbrā, or Sharafā for one, and Ṣafūriyā, Ṣafūrāʾ, or Ṣafīrāʾ for the other; al-Kashshāf calls the younger Ṣafīrāʾ and elder Ṣafrāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r7.anchor: اسم إحداهما قيل ليا وقيل عبرا وقيل شرفا واسم الأخرى قيل صفوريا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r8.claim: The most apparent sense is that they kept their sheep from the well for fear of the stronger shepherds.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r8.anchor: كانتا تمنعان غنمهما عن الماء خوفا من السقاة الأقوياء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say the women held their flocks back from the water out of fear of the powerful watering men.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r9.anchor: خوفا من السقاة الأقوياء قال ابن عباس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj is cited for the view that they kept their sheep from approaching the well to prevent them mixing with other flocks.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r10.anchor: وقيل تمنعان غنمهما عن التقدم إلى البئر لئلا تختلط بغيرها وحكي ذلك عن الزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r11.claim: Qatāda says they were keeping people away from their flock.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة : تمنعان الناس عن غنمهما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r12.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says they restrained the sheep so they would not scatter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء : تحبسان غنمهما عن أن تتفرق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r13.claim: The suggestion that the women were warding off spectators' gazes to cover their faces is, in al-Ālūsī's view, untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r13.anchor: وقيل تذودان عن وجوههما نظر الناظرين لتسترهما وهذا كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r14.claim: Mā khaṭbukumā asks what business or need caused their delay and restraint when they were not watering like the others; khaṭb is a verbal noun used for the object sought.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r14.anchor: أي ما مخطوبكما ومطلوبكما مما أنتما عليهما من التأخر والذود

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r15.claim: Moses's question shows that speaking to an unrelated woman is permissible when the matter is pertinent.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r15.anchor: وفي سؤاله عليه السلام إياهما دليل على جواز مكالمة الأجنبية فيما يعني

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r16.speaker: شمر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r16.claim: Shammar reads the khāʾ with kasra, taking the question to ask about their husband and why he does not water; al-Ālūsī says the objection raised against this reading is unclear and unanswered.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r16.anchor: وقرأ شمر ( ما خطبكما ) بكسر الخاء قال في البحر : أي من زوجكما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r17.claim: Some defend the common reading by taking khaṭb as the thing sought or requested, comparable to ḥubb meaning the beloved.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#3/r17.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الخطب فيها بمعنى المخطوب والمطلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r1.claim: The women describe their usual practice: they wait until the shepherds send their animals away because they cannot compete with them, rather than saying they will not water on that particular day until then.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r1.anchor: أي عادتنا أن لانسقي حتى يصرف الرعاة مواشيهم بعد ريها عن الماء عجزا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r2.speaker: ابن مصرف
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r2.claim: Ibn Muṣarrif reads the nūn with ḍamma, using the causative form asqā instead of the common form saqā.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مصرف ( لانسقي ) نضم النون من الاسقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAmr, along with the other listed readers, read yuṣdira with an open yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl, meaning the shepherds depart with their flocks.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r3.anchor: والعربيان : ابن عامر وأبو عمرو ( يصدر ) بفتح الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r4.claim: One explanation contrasts the readings: the open-yāʾ reading emphasizes the women's modesty and avoidance of men, while the ḍamma-yāʾ reading has the shepherds drive the animals off without implying that the men themselves leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r4.anchor: فأجيب بأن قراءة يصدر بفتح الياء تدل على فرط حيائها وتواريهما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r5.claim: Other recitations pronounce the consonant as pure zāy or as a sound between ṣād and zāy.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r5.anchor: وقريء بزاي خالصة وبحرف بين الصاد والزاي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r6.claim: A variant has ḍamma on rāʾ; the familiar plural pattern faʿāl has kasra, while ḍamma is irregular and may be a collective noun, an original plural, or a plural with a changed vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r6.anchor: وقريء الرعاء بضم الراء والمعروف في صيغ الجمع فعال بكسر الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r7.speaker: صدر الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r7.claim: A cited mnemonic poem lists exceptional fuʿāl plurals such as ربّاب، فرار، تؤام، عرام، عراق، رخال، ظؤار، and بساط; al-Ālūsī says its author is Ṣadr al-Afāḍil, not al-Zamakhsharī as sometimes claimed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r7.anchor: وقد نظمها صدر الأفاضل لا الزمخشري على الأصح بقوله : ما سمعنا كلما غير ثمان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān also considers the common plural riʿāʾ non-analogical: an agent adjective rāʿin would regularly pluralize as quḍāt, not this form.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r8.anchor: وذهب أبو حيان إلى أن الرعاء في قراءة الجمهور ليس بقياس أيضا قال : لأنه جمع راع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r9.speaker: عياش عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r9.claim: ʿAyyāsh from Abū ʿAmr reads riʿāʾ with fatḥa on rāʾ, either as a verbal noun used adjectivally for singular and plural or with an omitted muḍāf meaning the people of herding.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60/r9.anchor: وقرأ عياش عن أبي عمرو الرعاء بفتح الراء وهو مصدر أقيم مقام الصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r1.claim: Some say the women excused themselves as weak and modest, unable to compete with men, with no man to help and an aged, enfeebled father, so they had to wait until the others finished.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r1.anchor: كأنهما قالتا : إنا امرأتان ضعيفتان مستورتان لا نقدر على مساجلة الرجال

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r2.claim: Some say Moses's gracious question sought their need and implicitly offered help; the women's reply supplied the reason for their delay and indirectly requested assistance.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه عليه السلام اخرج السؤال على ما يقتضيه كرمه ورحمته بالضعفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r3.claim: Another view finds no explicit statement of weakness: the words signal modesty, and their father handled the task before age and frailty forced the daughters to take it up.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : ليس في الكلام ما يدل على ضعفهما بل فيه أمارات على حيائهما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī's preferred explanation is that they conveyed inability to compete because of both weakness and their natural modesty, even though the wording does not explicitly state weakness.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r4.anchor: ولعل الأولى أن يقال : إنهما أرادتا إظهار العجز عن المساجلة للضعف ولما جبلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r5.claim: The clause about their father may coordinate with an omitted clause or function circumstantially: they wait until the shepherds depart while their father is old.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن تكون حالا أي نترك السقي حتى يصدر الرعاء والحال أبونا شيخ كبير

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r6.claim: Most exegetes identify the women's father as the prophet Shuʿayb.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r6.anchor: وأبوهما عند أكثر المفسرين شعيب عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r7.claim: A prophet's allowing his daughters to water sheep is not forbidden by religion; judgments of propriety vary with custom, between Bedouin and urban life, and with necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r7.anchor: أن الأمر في نفسه ليس بمحظور فالدين لا يأباه وأما المروءة فالناس مختلفون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, in reports collected by Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, says Moses's employer was Athrūn, Shuʿayb's nephew; Abū Ḥayyān gives Hārūn instead of Athrūn, and al-Ḥasan gives Marwān.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r8.anchor: فأخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي عبيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r9.speaker: وهب وسعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī transmits from Wahb and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr a version identifying the father as Shuʿayb's nephew, like Abū ʿUbayda's view as quoted by Abū Ḥayyān.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r9.anchor: وحكى الطبرسي عن وهب وسعيد بن جبير نحو ما حكاه أبو حيان عن أبي عبيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says he had heard that the father was Shuʿayb's nephew named Raʿāwīl; a reliable informant said scripture calls him Yathrūn, priest or learned authority of Midian.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج أنه قال بلغني أن أبا الامرأتين ابن أخي شعيب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to call the employer Yathrib, master of Midian, and in another version Yathrūn, without specifying a relationship to Shuʿayb.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس أنه قال الذي استأجر موسى عليه السلام يثرب صاحب مدين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r12.claim: Other possibilities are that the man named in those reports was Shuʿayb's nephew or an unrelated person, or that the father was a righteous man unrelated to Shuʿayb.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r12.anchor: فيحتمل أن المسمى بما فيها ابن اخيه ويحتمل أنه رجل أجنبي عنه فقد قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r13.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r13.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī reports a view that Yathrūn was Shuʿayb himself; a person of the People of the Book told al-Ālūsī that their form is Yathro without final nūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r13.anchor: وحكى الطبرسي عن بعضهم أن يثرون اسم شعيب وقد أخبرني بعض أهل الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r14.speaker: التوراة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī's translation of Exodus 2 says Midian's priest had seven daughters, whom Moses helped water after shepherds drove them off; Exodus 3 calls Moses shepherd to Jethro, his father-in-law and priest of Midian.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r14.anchor: وكان لامام مدين سبع بنات فجاءت ودلت وملأت الاحواض لسقي غنم أبيهن

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r15.claim: A view cited in al-Baḥr says the daughters' uncle owned the flock and arranged the marriage, but they called him father because he was like one to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r15.anchor: قيل : كان عمها صاحب الغنم وهو المزوج عبرت عنه بالأب إذ كان بمثابته

ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī says such historical claims require a reliable report, notes the reports conflict without a clear strongest version, and follows the majority view that their actual father was Shuʿayb until evidence warrants departure.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p60#2/r16.anchor: فالمدار في قبول شيء من ذلك خبر يعول عليه والاخبار التي وقفنا عليها في هذا المطلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.claim: The water of Midian was a well from which people watered their livestock; a crowd was there watering animals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.anchor: وهو بئر كانوا يسقون منها مواشيهم، {وجد عليه أمة} جماعة {من الناس يسقون} مواشيهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.claim: The women held their sheep back from the water until the crowd finished and the well was clear for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.anchor: يعني: تحبسان وتمنعان أغنامهما عن الماء حتى يفرغ الناس وتخلو لهم البئر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the women kept their flocks from mixing with other people’s flocks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: تكفان الغنم عن أن تختلط بأغنام الناس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.claim: Qatada says the women were keeping people away from their flocks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: تكفان الناس عن أغنامهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.claim: Another view is that they kept their sheep from straying; the author prefers the first explanation because of what follows.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.claim: Moses asks why they are not watering their flocks with the others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.anchor: {قال} يعني: موسى للمرأتين، {ما خطبكما} ما شأنكما لا تسقيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read yusdir with open ya and damma on dal, intransitive: until the shepherds return from the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، وأبو عمرو، وابن عامر: "يصدر" بفتح الياء وضم الدال على اللزوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.claim: The other readers use the transitive form, meaning until the shepherds drive their animals away from the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: بضم الياء وكسر الدال، أي: حتى يصرفوا هم مواشيهم عن الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.claim: Al-riʿaʾ is the plural of raʿin, like tajir and tujjar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r9.anchor: و"الرعاء" جمع راع، مثل: تاجر وتجار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.claim: The women cannot manage watering alone or compete with men, so they wait, then use the water their flocks left in the trough.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199#2/r10.anchor: لأنا امرأتان لا نطيق أن نسقي، ولا نستطيع أن نزاحم الرجال، فإذا صدروا سقينا مواشينا ما أفضلت مواشيهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r1.claim: Their father could not water his animals because he was very old, so they had to tend the flocks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r1.anchor: لا يقدر أن يسقي مواشيه، فلذلك احتجنا نحن إلى سقي الغنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r2.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Hasan identify the women’s father as the prophet Shuʿayb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r2.anchor: والحسن: هو شعيب النبي عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه وسعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih and Saʿid ibn Jubayr say he was Yathrun, Shuʿayb’s nephew; Shuʿayb died blind and was buried between the Maqam and Zamzam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r3.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه، وسعيد بن جبير: هو يثرون (1) بن أخي شعيب، وكان شعيب قد مات قبل ذلك بعدما كف بصره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p200/r4.claim: Another view says the father was a man who had believed in Shuʿayb.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r1.claim: Moses asks what important affair or need is behind the women keeping their sheep away from the water.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says khatb is asked about a calamity or someone oppressed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r2.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والسؤال بالخطب إنما يكون في مصاب أو مضطهد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r3.claim: The women mean that they do not water their livestock; the object is omitted because it is understood.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r4.claim: They wait until the shepherds leave the water so their flocks will not mix with the men’s.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r4.anchor: عن الماء لئلا يخالطهم - هذا على قراءة أبي عمرو

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r5.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read the verb in the triliteral form with open yāʾ and damma on dāl; the others use the form with damma and kasra, with a different sense of driving the flock back.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r5.anchor: على قراءة أبي عمرو وابن عامر بفتح الياء وضم الدال ثلاثيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r6.claim: Their father’s age leaves them to water the flock; their youth suggests they have no brothers who could do it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r6.anchor: أن لهما أبا , وأن لا إخوة لهما وإلا لكفوهما ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r7.claim: They explain that their father cannot water because of age, and that sending his daughters is not forbidden; propriety varies by custom and circumstance, especially under necessity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r7.anchor: وهذا اعتذار أيضا عن كون أبيهم أرسلهما لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r18.claim: The two prophets’ material hardship makes them models: deprivation can preserve and honor the righteous, raise their rank, and teach disregard for this world.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r18.anchor: فانظر إلى هذين النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p476/r19.claim: The story urges good works, cooperation in virtue, and generous help despite one’s own exertion.

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses arrived so emaciated that the green fodder in his belly could be seen through him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : ولما ورد ماء مدين قال : ورد الماء حتى انه ليتراءى خضرة البقل من الهزال في بطنه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses walked eight nights from Egypt to Midian, a distance compared with Basra to Kufa, ate only tree leaves, went barefoot, and wore the skin of his feet away.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ان ابن عباس قال : لما خرج موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم من مصر إلى مدين وبينه وبينها ثمان ليال

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : امة من الناس قال : اناس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses ummah as a group of people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r4.anchor: حدثني سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : وجد عليه امة من الناس يقول : قوما

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says ummah here means a large number of people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r5.anchor: عن السدي وجد عليه امة من الناس يقول : كثرة من الناس يسقون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r6.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses arrived in fear, without provisions, servants, or a mount, and came upon people with livestock and sheep at Midian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : فخرج موسى بغير زاد ولا خدم ولا ظهر خائفا يترقب حتى وقع إلى امة من الناس بمدين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r7.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains that Moses found two women apart from the people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r7.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق يعني قوله : ووجد من دونهم امراتين اي وجد امراتين دون القوم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the women were holding their sheep back.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ووجد من دونهم امراتين تذودان يعني بذلك حابستين غنمهما

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Suddī are reported to give the same gloss: the women held their sheep back.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2961/r9.anchor: وروي ، عن سعيد بن جبير والسدي نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r1.claim: Abū Mālik says the women held their sheep until the people finished and the well was clear for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك في قوله : تذودان قال : تحبسان غنمهما حتى يفرغ الناس ويخلو لهما البئر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r2.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r2.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī says they kept their flock bunched together.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا عمران الجوني يقول في هذه الاية : ووجد من دونهم امراتين تذودان قال : تكفان اغنامهما بعضها على بعض

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they prevented their sheep from reaching the water.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج قوله : امراتين تذودان قال : تمنعان الغنم من الماء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that Moses asked why the women stood apart instead of watering with the people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما خطبكما قال : فقال لهما : ما خطبكما معتزلتين لا تسقيان مع الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r5.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses felt compassion and concern for the women when he saw them apart while the crowd dominated access to the water; he asked what their situation was.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ووجد امراتين من دون القوم تذودان غنمهما ، عن الماء ، وهو ماء مدين ، فوجد لهما رحمة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the women had no strength to compete with the men for water.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : قالتا لا نسقي قالتا : ليس لنا قوة نزاحم القوم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r7.claim: Qatada says they could not water until the people had watered, after which they would collect what remained.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي اي لا نستطيع ان نسقي حتى يسقي الناس ثم نتتبع فضالتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r8.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's account, the well was covered in winter and uncovered in summer; Moses lifted a huge stone that a hundred men could not lift, surprising the women, then watered their flock.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2962/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ولما ورد ماء مدين ان موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه امة من الناس يسقون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the women waited for the leftover water in the troughs because they could not compete with the men.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس فقال لهما : ما خطبكما معتزلتين لا تسقيان مع الناس ، فقالتا : ليس لنا قوة نزاحم القوم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses pitied the women because their father was old and removed the great stone over the well, which a group of Midianites normally lifted together.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r2.anchor: عن السدي قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وابونا شيخ كبير فرحمهما موسى فاتى إلى البئر فاقتلع صخرة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r3.claim: ʿUmar reports that after the crowd replaced the stone, which ten men could lift, Moses raised it and drew only one bucket, enough to water the flock.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب ان موسى عليه السلام لما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه امة من الناس يسقون قال : فلما فرغوا اعادوا الصخرة على البئر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r4.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the women could not overpower the men.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r4.anchor: عن محمد ابن اسحاق قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء امراتان لا نستطيع نغلب الرجال

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r5.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says their father could neither manage the task himself nor water his livestock, so they waited for the crowd; Moses took a bucket, used his strength to get through the crowd, and watered for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2964/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق وابونا شيخ كبير لا يقدر على ان يغني ذلك من نفسه ولا يسقي ماشيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r2.claim: His arrival at Midian’s water means that he reached the land of Midian; warada here means arriving or reaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r2.anchor: يدل قوله { لما ورد ماء مدين } أنه بلغ أرض مدين ، وذلك حين ورد ماءهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r3.claim: ‘Water’ means the watering place: tribes settled near water and used a tribe’s water-name as a name for its territory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r3.anchor: وماء القوم هو الذي تعرف به ديارهم لأن القبائل كانت تقطن عند المياه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r4.claim: A newcomer would head to the water because it gathered people, making it a natural place to find companions and a host.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r4.anchor: يناسب الغريب إذا جاء ديار قوم أن يقصد الماء لأنه مجتمع الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r5.claim: لَمَّا marks the time when one event occurs in relation to another: when Moses reached Midian, he found a group there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r5.anchor: و { لما } حرف توقيت وجود شيء بوجود غيره ، أي عندما حل بأرض مدين وجد أمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r6.claim: Ummah here means a large group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r6.anchor: والأمة : الجماعة الكثيرة العدد ، وتقدم في قوله تعالى { كان الناس أمة واحدة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r7.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf, following Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz, explains the omitted object of yasqūn as deliberately general—livestock or people—because the focus is the women’s withdrawal, not what was being watered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r7.anchor: كما في ( الكشاف ) تبعا ( لدلائل الإعجاز ) ، فيكون من تنزيل الفعل المتعدي منزلة اللازم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r8.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r8.claim: Al-Sakkākī, supported by his commentators al-Saʿd and al-Sayyid, instead treats the omitted object as an ellipsis for brevity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r8.anchor: كما اختاره السكاكي وأيده شارحاه السعد والسيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r9.speaker: الشيخان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r9.claim: For the omitted objects of ‘they hold back,’ ‘we give no water,’ and ‘he watered for them,’ Ibn ʿĀshūr says the two Shaykhs’ analysis is required; he finds no Qur’anic basis for the alternative elaboration by the author of al-Miftāḥ and his commentators, which depends on Israelite books to infer sheep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r9.anchor: فيتعين فيها ما ذهب إليه الشيخان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r10.claim: Min dūnihim means at a place farther from the crowd; dun originally describes what is lower, extended metaphorically to the direction reached after another place, as if walking down to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r10.anchor: ومعنى { من دونهم } في مكان غير المكان الذي حول الماء ، أي في جانب مباعد للأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r1.claim: The noun described by dūn is omitted through frequent use, leaving dūn to function like that missing noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r1.anchor: ويحذف الموصوف ب ( دون ) لكثرة الاستعمال فيصير ( دون ) بمنزلة ذلك الاسم المحذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r2.claim: Min with dūn can mark location, as in the Friday call, or mean ‘at’ according to Abū ʿUbayda’s usage; here it places the women away from the watering crowd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r2.anchor: وحرف { من } مع ( دون ) يجوز أن يكون للظرفية مثل { إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r3.claim: Dhawd literally drives livestock away from water; the word also figuratively applies to driving people away, as in the Prophetic report about people turned from his basin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r3.anchor: وحقيقة الذود طرد الأنعام عن الماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r4.claim: A Prophetic report speaks of people being driven away from the Prophet’s basin, an extended use of the verb for driving livestock from water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله في الحديث ( فليذادن أقوام عن حوضي ) الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r5.claim: The women were keeping their livestock from the water; given that Shuʿayb had sheep, the wording may be figurative or may use dhawḏ for all livestock, though lexicographers do not clearly settle its exact scope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r5.anchor: وفي التوراة : أن شعيبا كان صاحب غنم وأن موسى رعى غنمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r6.claim: The question is a substitution explaining the circumstance of finding the two women apart from the crowd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r6.anchor: وجملة { قال ما خطبكما } بدل اشتمال من جملة { ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r7.claim: Khaṭb means an important matter or event; Moses asks about their story and why they came to the water but did not approach to water their flock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r7.anchor: والخطب : الشأن والحدث المهم ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى { قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r8.claim: They avoid watering while the place is crowded and continue waiting until the shepherds depart; the imperfect verb presents their abstention as continuing until then.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r8.anchor: فأجابتا بأنهما كرهتا أن تسقيا في حين اكتظاظ المكان بالرعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r9.claim: Al-riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿī, ‘shepherd.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r10.claim: Iṣdār means making the shepherds depart after watering, that is, sending them away with their animals so the crowd clears.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r10.anchor: والإصدار : الإرجاع عن السقي ، أي حتى يسقي الرعاء ويصدروا مواشيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r11.claim: Their not pushing into the crowd reflects their good manners and fine upbringing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p99/r11.anchor: وصدهما عن المزاحمة عادتهما لأنهما كانتا ذواتي مروءة وتربية زكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r1.claim: The majority read yuṣdir, with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl, making it causative: the shepherds send their animals away from the water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { يصدر } بضم الياء وكسر الدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar read yaṣduru with fatḥa on the prefix and ḍamma on dāl, assigning the intransitive return from the water to the shepherds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r2.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر { يصدر } بفتح حرف المضارعة وضم الدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r3.claim: The second reading implies that the women water their animals every day, but the verse itself does not establish this as a daily habit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r3.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن تلك عادتهما كل يوم سقي ، وليس في اللفظ دلالة على أنه عادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r4.claim: Their father’s age excuses their watering among men: they have no other man to draw water for them, and he is too weak to compete at the well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r4.anchor: وكان قولهما { وأبونا شيخ كبير } اعتذارا عن حضورهما للسقي مع الرجال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r5.speaker: ابن العبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿIbrī says Jethro son of Reuel had seven daughters, two of whom went to water; he concludes that Jewish tradition identifies Shuʿayb as Jethro.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r5.anchor: وقال ابن العبري في ( تاريخه ) : يثرون بن رعويل له سبع بنات خرج للسقي منهما اثنتان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r6.claim: Exodus first calls their father Reuel and later Jethro, Moses’s father-in-law; Ibn ʿĀshūr regards these as names of the same man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r6.anchor: وسماه في ذلك السفر أول مرة رعويل ثم أعاد الكلام عليه فسماه يثرون ووصفه بحمي موسى ، فالمسمى واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r7.claim: Calling a prophet a priest reflects Jewish usage: a priest foretells the unseen and the term can denote a Jewish religious official.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r7.anchor: والتعبير عن النبي بالكاهن اصطلاح . لأن الكاهن يخبر عن الغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r8.claim: Since Muslim scholars identify the father as the messenger Shuʿayb, they treat his conduct as revealed prior law, applicable unless abrogated, and derive several rulings from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r8.anchor: وللجزم بأنه شعيب الرسول جعل علماؤنا ما صدر منه في هذه القصة شرعا سابقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r9.claim: The precedent supports women working for a livelihood, required modesty, paternal guardianship in marriage, physical work as a dower, combining marriage and hire in one contract, and the lawfulness of hiring; al-Qurṭubī discusses these fully.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r9.anchor: ومنها مباشرة المرأة الأعمال والسعي في طرق المعيشة ، ووجوب استحيائها ، وولاية الأب في النكاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r10.claim: The father’s permission shows a woman may manage her property and appear publicly while covering what must be covered, if prior law is reported without abrogation; public reserve varies with custom and society.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p100/r10.anchor: وفي إذنه لابنتيه بالسقي دليل على جواز معالجة المرأة أمور مالها وظهورها في مجامع الناس

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r1.claim: Wurūd means coming to water; its opposite, ṣudūr, is returning from it.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r1.anchor: الورود إتيان الماء وضده الصدور وهو

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r2.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r2.claim: Al-Mufradat says wurūd originally means heading for water, then came to be used more broadly.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r2.anchor: وفي "المفردات" : الورود أصله قصد الماء ثم يستعمل في غيره

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r3.claim: Moses reached the well of Midian, three miles or less from the town, where people watered their livestock.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r3.anchor: والمعنى ولما وصل موسى وجاء {ماء مدين} وهو بئر على طرف المدينة

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses arrived so emaciated from hunger that green vegetable matter could be seen through his belly.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ورده وإنه ليتراءى خضرة البقل في بطنه من الهزال

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r5.claim: Moses found a large group watering their animals by the well.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r5.anchor: أي جانب البئر وفوق شفيرها {أمة من الناس} جماعة كثيرة منهم

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r6.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r6.claim: The two women were Shafuriyya and Layya, daughters of Yathrun, whom al-Suhayli identifies as Shuayb.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r6.anchor: صفورياء وليا ابنتا يثرون ويثرون هو شعيب قاله السهيلي في كتاب "التعريف"

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r7.claim: Tadhūdān means restraining, turning back, or pushing their sheep away from the well.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r7.anchor: الذود والكف والطرد والدفع أي تمنعان أغنامهما عن التقدم إلى البئر

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r8.claim: Al-Kashifi says Moses went over to them because prophets have innate compassion, and did so gently.

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r9.claim: Khatb is an important matter that prompts much discussion; Moses asks why they are holding back and not watering like the others.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r9.anchor: الخطب الأمر العظيم الذي يكثر فيه التخاطب أي ما شأنكما فيما أنتما عليه من التأخر والذود

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r10.claim: Some ask how Moses could speak to two unrelated women; the answer is that he was safe from temptation and protected from it.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم : كيف استجاز موسى أن يكلم امرأتين أجنبيتين والجواب كان آمنا على نفسه معصوما من الفتنة

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r11.claim: The analogy is that the Prophet could marry without witnesses because he was protected from denying or being accused of denying the marriage.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r11.anchor: كان للرسول التزوج بامرأة من غير الشهود لأن الشهود لصيانة العقد عن التجاحد

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r12.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿin, like qiyām and qāʾim; marʿā is pasture, and a caretaker of people or animals is a rāʿin.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r12.anchor: والرعاء بالكسر جمع راع كقيام جمع قائم ما يرعاء والمرعى موضع الرعي

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r13.claim: A hadith says everyone is responsible for those in their care; some distinguish animal herders from human shepherds, meaning rulers.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r13.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كلكم مسؤول عن رعيته" قيل : الرعاء هم الذين يرعون المواشي والرعاة هم الذين يرعون الناس

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r14.claim: The women waited until the shepherds took their animals away after watering, avoiding competition and mixing with men, then watered with what remained.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r14.anchor: حذرا من مخالطة الرجال فإذا انصرفوا سقينا من فضل مواشيهم

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r15.claim: Objects of watering, restraining, and sending away are omitted because the actions themselves matter and motivated Moses to help them.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r15.anchor: وحذف مفعول السقي والذود والإصدار لما أن الغرض هو بيان تلك الأفعال أنفسها

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r16.claim: Their father, Shuayb, was old or great in rank and honor; unable to go out, he had to send them to tend and water the animals.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r16.anchor: كبير السن أو القدر والشرف لا يستطيع أن يخرج فيرسلنا للرعي والسقي اضطرارا

BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r17.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r17.claim: A contemporary who sees a lesson in the unnoticed livestock of a prophet grasps it: herdsmen may not recognize prophets, as villagers may not know prophetic law, and believers are few.
BURSEVI:v6p286#5/r17.anchor: ومن قال من المعاصرين فيه عبرة أن مواشي النبي لم يلتفت إليها فقد أتى بالعبرة لأن الراعي لا يعرف ما النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r2.claim: Moses reached Midian's water without entering it; warada can mean entering a place or merely arriving at it, as in 19:71.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r2.anchor: معناه بلغه لا أنه دخل فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r3.claim: Midian is indeclinable because it is the name of a known town.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r3.anchor: ومدين لا ينصرف إذ هي بلدة معروفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r4.claim: Umma means a large group, and yasqun here means watering their livestock.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r5.claim: Min dunihim places the women on Moses' side; he reached them before the crowd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r5.anchor: ومن دونهم، معناه ناحية إلى الجهة التي جاء منها فوصل إلى «المرأتين»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r6.claim: Tadhuddan means to prevent or hold back, as in the Prophet's saying that men will be driven away from his basin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r6.anchor: وتذودان معناه تمنعان وتحبسان، ومنه قوله عليه السلام «فليذادن رجال عن حوضي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r7.speaker: بعض المصاحف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r7.claim: Some codices read امرأتين حابستين تذودان.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r8.speaker: عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r8.claim: Abbas and others say the women kept their sheep from water, fearing stronger shepherds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r8.anchor: واختلف في المذود، فقال عباس وغيره تذودان غنمهما عن الماء خوفا من السقاة الأقوياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r9.claim: Qatada says the women kept people away from their flock.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة تذودان الناس عن غنمهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r10.claim: Khatb is typically asked about calamity, oppression, someone needing sympathy, or unusual wrongdoing, presenting their situation as trouble.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r10.anchor: وكان استعمال السؤال بالخطب إنما هو في مصاب أو مضطهد أو من يشفق عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r11.claim: Their old father could not tend the flock; they were too weak to contend with men and waited until shepherds left and the water was free.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r11.anchor: وأن أباهما شيخ كبير فالمعنى أنه لا يستطيع لضعفه أن يباشر أمر غنمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r12.claim: One group says the wells were open but the crowd kept the women away; Moses pushed through and watered for them, explaining praise of his strength.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r12.anchor: وقالت فرقة كانت الآبار مكشوفة وكان زحم الناس يمنعهما، فلما أراد موسى أن يسقي لهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r13.claim: Another group says the women collected leftovers while Moses lifted a stone covering a well; reports say seven, ten, thirty, or forty people were needed to lift it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل كانت آبارهم على أفواهها حجارة كبار وكان ورود المرأتين تتبع ما في صهاريج الشرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r16.speaker: الجمهور وطلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r16.claim: Most pronounce the n in نسقي with fatḥa; Talha pronounces it with damma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r16.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «نسقي» بفتح النون، وقرأ طلحة «نسقي» بضمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r17.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر والحسن وأبو جعفر وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r17.claim: They read يصدر with open yā and damma on dāl, intransitively: the shepherds depart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r17.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر «حتى يصدر» بفتح الياء وضم الدال وهي قراءة الحسن وأبي جعفر وقتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r18.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r18.claim: The other reading has yā with damma and dāl with kasra, deleting the object: they send their livestock back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r18.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «يصدر» بضم الياء وكسر الدال على حذف المفعول تقديره مواشيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r1.claim: Object deletion is common in Qur'anic usage and speech; al-Aʿraj, Talha, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Isa also have this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r1.anchor: وهي قراءة الأعرج وطلحة والأعمش وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p284/r2.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿin, shepherd.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r7.claim: Al-ummah here means a group, namely the shepherds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r1.claim: The people watering their livestock were shepherds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r1.anchor: يسقون مواشيهم ووجد من دونهم أي من سوى الأمة امرأتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r2.claim: The two women were Shuʿayb's daughters; Muqatil names the elder Ṣabura and the younger ʿAbra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r2.anchor: وهما ابنتا شعيب قال مقاتل واسم الكبرى صبورا والصغرى عبرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says they were holding their sheep back; the word sheep is omitted for brevity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي تكفان غنمهما فحذف الغنم اختصارا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r4.claim: The commentators say the women waited for the crowd to leave and the well to clear before watering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون وإنما فعلتا ذلك ليفرغ الناس وتخلو لهما البئر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r5.claim: Moses asks what their situation is and why they are not watering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r5.anchor: قال موسى ما خطبكما أي ما شأنكما لا تسقيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو الجوزاء وابن يعمر وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r6.claim: These readers pronounce the nūn of nasqī with ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو الجوزاء وابن يعمر وابن السميفع ﴿ لا نسقي ﴾ برفع النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r7.claim: These readers pronounce yaṣduru with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl, meaning the shepherds return.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو حعفر يصدر بفتح الياء وضم الدال أي حتى يرجع الرعاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r8.speaker: الباقون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r8.claim: The other readers pronounce yuṣdiru with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl, meaning the shepherds drive their flocks away from the water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r8.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ﴿ يصدر ﴾ بضم الياء وكسرالدال أرادوا حتى يرد الرعاء غنمهم عن الماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r9.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿ, as ṣāḥib has the plural ṣiḥāb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r9.anchor: والرعاء جمع راع كما يقال صاحب وصحاب وقرأ عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r10.speaker: عكرمة وسعيد بن جبير وابن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r10.claim: These readers pronounce riʿāʾ with ḍamma on rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r10.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وسعيد بن جبير وابن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري الرعاء بضم الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r11.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r11.claim: The women explain that two women cannot compete with the men, and their elderly father is too old to water the livestock, so they have had to do it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r11.anchor: والمعنى نحن امرأتان لا نستطيع أن نزاحم الرجال وأبونا شيخ كبير لا يقدر أن يسقي ماشيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r12.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r12.claim: A huge rock covered the well; once the shepherds finished and replaced it, the women watered their sheep from the leftover basins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p212/r12.anchor: وكان على تلك البئر صخرة عظيمة فاذا فرغ الرعاء من سقيهم أعادوا الصخرة فتأتي المرأتان

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r1.claim: A person should flee with their faith and rely on their Lord.
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على أن الواجب على المرء الفرار بدينه، والتوكل على ربه.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r2.claim: The passage commends helping the weak.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r4.claim: Unrelated men may speak with women when needed and when safe from temptation or harm to themselves.
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: (قال ما خطبكما) على إباحة كلام الأجنبيات عند الحاجة والأمن على النفس.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r5.claim: The phrase about their elderly father models tactful asking.
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: (من خير فقير) على تلطف في السؤال.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r7.claim: The story gives glad tidings of deliverance from oppressors.
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r7.anchor: وتدل على بشارة بالنجاة من الظلمة.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r8.claim: The story's deliverance and provision are blessings.

JISHUMI:v8p5487/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r9.claim: Oppression is a human act, making escape from it a meaningful means of salvation.
JISHUMI:v8p5487/r9.anchor: وتدل أن الظلم فعل العبد؛ ليصح النجاة بالهرب [*].

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r1.claim: The water of Midian was the source from which its people drew; reports identify it as a well.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r1.anchor: { ماء مدين } ماءهم الذي يستقون منه ، وكان بئرا فيما روي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r2.claim: Wurud means coming to and reaching the water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r2.anchor: ووروده : مجيئه والوصول إليه { وجد عليه }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r3.claim: He found the people above the well, at its rim and watering place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r3.anchor: { وجد عليه } وجد فوق شفيره ومستقاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r4.claim: The group is a large crowd, and its people are drawn from different communities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r4.anchor: { أمة } جماعة كثيفة العدد { من الناس } من أناس مختلفين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r5.claim: The two women were at a lower place than the crowd.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r5.anchor: { من دونهم } في مكان أسفل من مكانهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r6.claim: The verb means driving away or pushing back; they held their flock back because the men at the water were stronger and prevented them from drawing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r6.anchor: والذود : الطرد والدفع وإنما كانتا تذودان ؛ لأن على الماء من هو أقوى منهما فلا يتمكنان من السقي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r7.claim: Other explanations say the women avoided crowding, kept their sheep apart from the men's flocks, or shielded their faces from onlookers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r8.claim: The question asks their situation; literally it asks what they seek, with خطب deriving from a sought matter, as شأن derives from intending a purpose.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r8.anchor: { ما خطبكما } ما شأنكما . وحقيقته : ما مخطوبكما ، أي : مطلوبكما من الزياد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r9.claim: Zamakhshari records variant vocalizations of لا نسقي, يصدر, and الرعاء.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r9.anchor: وقرىء ( لا نسقي ) و ( يصدر ) . و ( الرعاء ) بضم النون والياء والراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r10.claim: الرعاء is a collective noun like الرخال and الثناء; the kasra vocalization follows the regular pattern of صيام and قيام.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r10.anchor: والرعاء : اسم جمع كالرخال والثناء . وأما الرعاء بالكسر فقياس ، كصيام وقيام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405/r11.anchor: { كبير } كبير السن { فسقى لهما } فسقى غنمهما لأجلهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.claim: The objects of these verbs are omitted because the actions of watering and holding back matter, regardless of what was watered or held back.
