KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.anchor: قلت : لأن الغرض هو الفعل لا المفعول . ألا ترى أنه إنما رحمهما لأنهما كانتا على الذياد وهم على السقي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.claim: Their answer explains that, as two weak, modest women without a man to help and with an aged father, they must wait until the men finish watering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.anchor: قلت : سألهما عن سبب الذود فقالتا : السبب في ذلك أنا امرأتاه ضعيفتان مستورتان لا نقدر على مساجلة الرجال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.claim: Shuayb's daughters tending livestock was not forbidden by religion; social standards vary across peoples, Bedouin and settled communities, especially in necessity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.anchor: قلت : الأمر في نفسه ليس بمحظور ، فالدين لا يأباه . وأما المروأة ، فالناس مختلفون في ذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses left Egypt for Midian, eight nights away, with no food but tree leaves; he traveled barefoot and his feet’s soles wore away before arrival.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما خرج موسى من مصر إلى مدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r6.claim: Umma here means a group of people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r6.anchor: وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the group numbered forty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r8.claim: The people were watering their sheep and livestock.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r8.anchor: ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r9.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r9.claim: Qutrub says tadhūdān means the women were holding something back; a poetic line compares this with driving off a herd of beasts.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r10.claim: A second lexical sense is to repel or drive away, illustrated by a verse about Banu Tamim taking a staff.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r1.claim: Abu Malik and al-Suddi say the women kept their sheep from the water because they were too weak to jostle through the crowd.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r1.anchor: تحبسان غنمهما عن الماء لضعفهما عن زحام الناس . قاله أبو مالك والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r2.claim: Qatada says the women were keeping people away from their flock.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنهما تذودان الناس عن غنمهما ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says they prevented their sheep from mixing with other people’s sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r3.anchor: تمنعان غنمهما أن تختلط بغنم الناس ، حكاه يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r4.claim: Khatb means their affair or situation; the word denotes a weighty matter, as does khuṭba because it concerns an important affair.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r4.anchor: أي ما شأنكما , وفي الخطب تضخيم الشيء ومنه الخطبة لأنها من الأمر المعظم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r5.claim: Ṣudūr means departing; ṣadr is so named because deliberation issues from it, and maṣdar because actions issue from it; riʿāʾ is the plural of shepherd.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r5.anchor: والصدور الانصراف , ومنه الصدر لأن التدبير يصدر عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r6.claim: One explanation for their waiting was modesty and avoiding contact with men.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r7.claim: The other explanation is that they were too weak to compete with the men and their livestock.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r8.claim: They may have mentioned their father’s age to excuse why they themselves tended the sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أنهما قالتا ذلك اعتذارا إلى موسى عن معاناتهما سقي الغنم بأنفسهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r9.claim: Alternatively, they mentioned their elderly father to move Moses to help them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p245/r9.anchor: الثاني : قالتا ذلك ترقيقا لموسى ليعاونهما

MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r1.claim: Umar reports that Moses arrived at a well where people watered; after the shepherds left, the two women said they could not water until then because their father was very old.
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r1.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب في قوله ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين ﴾ قال إن موسى

MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r2.claim: Umar says the shepherds replaced a rock over the well, which only ten men could lift; Moses moved it alone.
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب في قوله ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين ﴾ قال إن موسى

MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r3.claim: Moses drew one bucket, watered the women's flock until it was full, and then went to the shade.
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب في قوله ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين ﴾ قال إن موسى

MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses' father-in-law was named Thirbi.
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان اسم ختن موسى ثيربي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r1.claim: Warada means arrived; the water was their well, used to water livestock.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r1.anchor: ماءهم الذي يسقون منه وكان بئرا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r2.claim: Moses found a group of different people watering livestock beside the well.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r2.anchor: على جانب البئر ﴿ أمة ﴾ جماعة ﴿ من الناس ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r3.claim: He found two women below or apart from the main group, keeping their sheep away from the water.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r4.claim: They kept the flock away because stronger people prevented them watering first, or to keep the sheep from mixing with other flocks; dhawdh means repel.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r4.anchor: لأن على الماء من هو أقوى منهما فلا تتمكنا من السقي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r5.claim: The question asks their affair or need, literally what they seek by holding their flock back.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r5.anchor: ما شأنكما وحقيقته ما مخطوبكما أي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r6.speaker: الشامي ويزيد وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r6.claim: Al-Shami, Yazid, and Abu Amr read yusdir, meaning the shepherds send their flocks back.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r6.anchor: مواشيهم يصدر شامى ويزيد وأبو عمر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r7.claim: Riʿa is the plural of raʿin, like qaim and qiyam.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r8.claim: Their father could not water or graze the sheep; kabir may describe his condition or age, explaining why the women water them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p232/r8.anchor: في حاله أو في السن لا يقدر على رعي الغنم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r1.claim: Moses walked until he reached Midian's water; here warada means arriving at the water, not entering it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r1.anchor: مشى موسى عليه السلام حتى ورد ماء مدين أي بلغها. ووروده الماء معناه بلغه لا أنه دخل فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r2.claim: Warada can mean entering something or merely seeing and reaching it; Moses reached this water without entering it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r2.anchor: ولفظة الورود قد تكون بمعنى الدخول في المورود، وقد تكون بمعنى الاطلاع عليه والبلوغ إليه وإن لم يدخل.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r3.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r3.claim: Zuhayr's verse about arriving at water provides poetic evidence for warada meaning reaching it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r3.anchor: ومنه قول زهير: فلما وردن الماء زرقا جمامه وضعن عصي الحاضر المتخيم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r4.claim: Qurṭubī says these senses of warada were discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r4.anchor: وقد تقدمت هذه المعاني في قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r5.claim: Madyan, as the name of a known town, is diptote.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r5.anchor: ومدين لا تنصرف إذ هي بلدة معروفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r6.claim: Madyan is also identified as a tribe descended from Madyan son of Abraham; Qurṭubī refers to an earlier discussion in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r6.anchor: وقيل: قبيلة من ولد مدين بن إبراهيم وقد مضى القول فيه في «الأعراف».

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r7.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r7.claim: An unnamed poet's line about Madyan is cited in connection with the place name.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: رهبان مدين لو رأوك تنزلوا والعصم من شعف الجبال الفادر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r8.claim: Umma means a large group of people.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r9.claim: The people were watering their livestock.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r10.claim: Min dūnihim means to the side in the direction from which Moses arrived, so he encountered the women before reaching the crowd.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r10.anchor: و { من دونهم } معناه ناحية إلى الجهة التي جاء منها، فوصل إلى المرأتين قبل وصوله إلى الأمة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r11.claim: Taḏūdān can mean holding back or restraining; the verb is also used of keeping men away from the Prophet's basin.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r12.claim: Some codices read the phrase as two women who were holding back, explicitly supplying ḥābisatayn.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r12.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف: { امرأتين حابستين تذودان }

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r13.claim: The root is used for restraining or holding something back.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r13.anchor: يقال: ذاد يذود إذا حبس. وذدت الشيء حبسته

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r14.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r14.claim: A poet's use of aḏūḏu for keeping a herd of wild animals back illustrates restraint.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r14.anchor: قال الشاعر: أبيت على باب القوافي كأنما أذود بها سربا من الوحش نزعا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r15.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r15.claim: Another poem uses taḏūd to mean driving away, checking, or warding off.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r15.anchor:
قال:
لقد سلبت عصاك بنو تميم
فما تدري بأي عصا تذود

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r16.speaker: ابن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r16.claim: Ibn Sallām says the women kept their sheep apart so they would not mix with other people's flocks, leaving the object implicit.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r16.anchor: ابن سلام: تمنعان غنمهما لئلا تختلط بغنم الناس فحذف المفعول

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r17.claim: The omitted object may be left vague to prompt the listener or omitted because it is already understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r17.anchor: إما إيهاما على المخاطب، وإما استغناء بعلمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the women held their sheep back from water for fear of powerful shepherds.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r18.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تذودان غنمهما عن الماء خوفا من السقاة الأقوياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r19.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r19.claim: Qatāda says the women kept people away from their sheep.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r20.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r20.claim: Al-Naḥḥās prefers the explanation that they kept their own sheep from mingling: waiting for the shepherds to leave otherwise would not explain delayed watering.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r20.anchor: قال النحاس: والأول أولى لأن بعده { قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء } ولو كانتا تذودان عن غنمهما الناس لم تخبرا عن سبب تأخير سقيهما حتى يصدر الرعاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r21.claim: Mā khaṭbukumā means what is your affair or situation?
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r21.anchor: فلما رأى موسى عليه السلام ذلك منهما { قال ما خطبكما } أي شأنكما

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r22.speaker: رؤبة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r22.claim: Ruʾba's verse uses khaṭb to mean an affair or matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23/r22.anchor: قال رؤبة: يا عجبا ما خطبه وخطبي

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r1.claim: Qatada says God sent Shuayb to the people of al-Aykah and Madyan; al-Qurtubi notes the dispute over Shuayb’s father’s name was discussed under al-Aʿraf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: بعث الله تعالى شعيبا إلى أصحاب الأيكة وأصحاب مدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the dispute about Shuayb’s father’s name was discussed earlier in al-Aʿraf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r2.anchor: وقد مضى في «الأعراف» الخلاف في اسم أبيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r1.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says a husband should not consummate before paying at least a quarter dinar; if he does, the marriage stands, and later Maliki scholars regard advancing all or part of the dowry as recommended.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r1.anchor: منع علماؤنا من الدخول حتى ينقد ولو ربع دينار قاله ابن القاسم. فإن دخل قبل أن ينقد مضى،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r2.claim: If the dowry was tending sheep, beginning the service counts as payment; if consummation waited until travel, delay without condition may last even for life.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r2.anchor: على أنه إن كان الصداق رعية الغنم فقد نقد الشروع في الخدمة وإن كان دخل حين سافر فطول الانتظار في النكاح جائز

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r3.claim: A stipulated delay is valid only for a sound purpose such as wedding preparations or waiting until a young bride is ready for consummation.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r3.anchor: وأما إن كان بشرط فلا يجوز إلا أن يكون الغرض صحيحا مثل التأهب للبناء وانتظار صلاحية الزوجة للدخول إن كانت صغيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r1.claim: Malik says a shepherd is a trustee, not liable for animals lost or stolen, and is believed absent evidence of betrayal or lying.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r1.anchor: قال مالك: وليس على الراعي ضمان وهو مصدق فيما هلك أو سرق لأنه أمين كالوكيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r2.claim: Kaʿb ibn Malik’s report from his father recounts how a girl slaughtered a dying sheep with a stone; the Prophet was asked and ordered them to eat it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r2.anchor: وساق حديث كعب بن مالك عن أبيه: أنه كانت لهم غنم ترعى بسلع، فأبصرت جارية لنا بشاة من غنمنا موتا فكسرت حجرا فذبحتها به،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r3.speaker: المهلب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r3.claim: Al-Muhallab says shepherds and agents are trusted regarding entrusted property until evidence of betrayal or falsehood appears; Malik and others agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r3.anchor: قال المهلب: فيه من الفقه تصديق الراعي والوكيل فيما ائتمنا عليه حتى يظهر عليهما دليل الخيانة والكذب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r4.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says a shepherd who slaughters a sheep fearing imminent death is not liable if he brings it slaughtered; another view holds him liable until he proves his explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: إذا خاف الموت على شاة فذبحها لم يضمن ويصدق إذا جاء بها مذبوحة. وقال غيره: يضمن حتى يبين ما قال.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says a shepherd who breeds the owner’s females without permission is not liable for loss because breeding develops the property.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r5.anchor: فقال ابن القاسم: لا ضمان عليه لأن الإنزاء من إصلاح المال ونمائه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r6.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r6.claim: Ashhab says the shepherd is liable for losses after breeding animals without permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r6.anchor: وقال أشهب: عليه الضمان وقول ابن القاسم أشبه بدليل حديث كعب،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi favors Ibn al-Qasim: a reliable shepherd is not liable for loss from conscientious judgment, though an owner may hold a known corrupt shepherd liable.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r7.anchor: وقول ابن القاسم أشبه بدليل حديث كعب، وأنه لا ضمان عليه فيما تلف عليه باجتهاده، إن كان من أهل الصلاح،

QASHANI:28:23-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r1.claim: The water of Midian is the source and spring of unveiling, secret knowledge, and spiritual converse.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r1.anchor: مورد علم المكاشفة ومنهل علم السر والمكالمة

QASHANI:28:23-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r2.claim: The people watering there may be saints and wayfarers in God, whose drink is unveiling and who give it to their powers and disciples.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r2.anchor: من الأولياء والسالكين في الله والمتوسطين الذين مشربهم من منهل المكاشفة

QASHANI:28:23-24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r3.claim: Alternatively, they are the sacred intellects and disembodied spirits of the realm of power, the true inhabitants of this spring, watering celestial and human souls and the cosmos.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r3.anchor: أو العقول المقدسة والأرواح المجردة من أهل الجبروت فإنها في الحقيقة أهل ذلك المنهل

QASHANI:28:23-24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r4.claim: The two women symbolize the theoretical and practical intellects, at a lower rank than the saints and spirits at the spring.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r4.anchor: من مرتبة أسفل من مرتبتهم { امرأتين } هما العاقلتان النظرية والعملية

QASHANI:28:23-24/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r5.claim: They hold the flock of faculties back from the spring because their sustenance is rational knowledge and practical philosophy; they lack unveiling until Moses the heart arrives.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r5.anchor: أغنام القوى عنه لكون مشربها من العلوم العقلية والحكمة العملية

QASHANI:28:23-24/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r6.claim: They drink from the holy spirits' and intellects' surplus when those shepherds depart from the spring and turn toward them, imparting its overflow.
QASHANI:28:23-24/r6.anchor: شربنا من فضلة رعاء الأرواح والعقول المقدسة عند صدورها عن المنهل متوجهة إلينا

QASHANI:28:23-24/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:23-24/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:23-24/r7.claim: Their father is the spirit, too great and old to undertake watering.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r2.claim: The water was the source from which people watered, reportedly a well; “arrived at it” means reached it, “at it” means by its rim and watering place, and the group was numerous and diverse.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r3.claim: “Below them” places the two women lower than the crowd; “tadhūdān” means to push away or hold back.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r3.anchor: الذود الدفع والطرد فقوله ( تذودان ) أي تحبسان

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the women held their sheep back because stronger people at the water prevented them from watering.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج لأن على الماء من كان أقوى منهما فلا يتمكنان من السقي

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r5.speaker: قول آخر
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r5.claim: One explanation is that they held their sheep back because they disliked competing for water.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r6.speaker: قول آخر
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that they kept their flock separate from the other people’s animals.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r7.speaker: قول آخر
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that they avoided mixing with the men.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r8.claim: A further reported interpretation is that they warded off onlookers so they would not look at their faces.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r8.anchor: كانتا تذودان عن وجوههما نظرا الناظر ليراهما

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation is that they kept people away from their flock.

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says they restrained the sheep so they would not scatter and wander off.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r10.anchor: قال الفراء تحبسانها عن أن تتفرق وتتسرب

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r11.claim: “What is your business?” literally asks what matter or request they are pursuing by holding the flock back; “khatb” is used as “shaʾn” is in “what is your affair?”
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r11.anchor: أي ما شأنكما وحقيقته ما مخطوبكما أي مطلوبكما من الذياد فسمى المخطوب خطبا

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r12.claim: Their answer shows weakness: women normally do not water, they had delayed their flock, awaited the herders’ departure and leftover water, and their elderly father could not come to do it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r12.anchor: وذلك يدل على ضعفهما عن السقي

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r13.claim: Moses watered for them before the herders left, so the women returned to their father earlier than usual.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r13.anchor: فعند ذلك سقى لهما قبل صدر الرعاء

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl: the herders themselves depart from the water.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r14.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم بفتح الياء

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r15.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r15.claim: The remaining readers use ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl: the herders make their animals depart from the water.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الياء ، وكسر الدال

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r1.claim: One explanation is that the women held back their flocks because they lacked the strength to get them to the water.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r1.anchor: because they were not strong enough to make their way to the water

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r2.claim: Another explanation is that they did not want their animals mixing with the others.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r2.anchor: because they did not want their animals to mix with the others

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r3.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r3.claim: Another explanation is modesty, to avoid mixing with the men watering their flocks.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r3.anchor: or out of modesty in order to avoid mingling with the men watering their flocks (Q, R)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r4.claim: Holding back is usually understood as holding the flocks back.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r4.anchor: the act of holding back is usually understood to mean they were holding the flocks back

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r5.claim: Ṭ says the women may instead have been holding the other people back from their flocks.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r5.anchor: they were holding the other people back from their flocks (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r6.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r6.claim: Ṭ says Moses asked why the women stayed away rather than watering their flocks.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r6.anchor: Moses asked them why they were staying away rather than watering their flocks (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r7.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r7.claim: Their reply means their father was too old to water the flocks; had he been present, they would not have had to stay back.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r7.anchor: their father was too old to do so himself, and had he been present, they would not have had to stay back with their flocks (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r8.claim: The question can also mean What is your situation? or What is going on with you?
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r8.anchor: can also be rendered, “What is your situation?” or“What is going on with you?”

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r9.claim: The plain sense is that Moses, as a strong man in that social setting, moved the animals forward and watered them.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r9.anchor: Moses, as a strong man in that particular social context, was able to move the animals forward and give them water

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r10.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r10.claim: Popular accounts say Moses lifted a rock too heavy for ten men that blocked another well, allowing the women's animals to drink.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r10.anchor: a heavy rock that ten men could not lift was blocking another well; Moses lifted it, allowing the women’s animals to drink (Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r11.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r11.claim: R says these popular accounts are often dismissed.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r11.anchor: such popular accounts are, however, often dismissed (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:23/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r12.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r12.claim: Most Muslims identify the women's father, called Jethro in the Bible, with the prophet Shuʿayb, although the Quran does not say this explicitly.
STUDYQURAN:28:23/r12.anchor: Most Muslims say that the father of the women, named Jethro in the Bible, was identical with the prophet Shuʿayb, though the Quran does not explicitly indicate this (R)

TAB-FULL:v18p206/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r1.claim: When Moses reached Midian’s water, he found a group of people watering their livestock.

TAB-FULL:v18p206/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses أمة as a large crowd of people watering.
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r2.anchor: عن السدي، " {وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون} [القصص: 23] يقول: كثرة من الناس يسقون

TAB-FULL:v18p206/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله " {أمة من الناس} [القصص: 23] قال: أناسا

TAB-FULL:v18p206/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the group consisted of people watering livestock and sheep at Midian.
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: «وقع إلى أمة من الناس يسقون بمدين أهل نعم وشاء»

TAB-FULL:v18p206/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas compares Midian’s water source to the local well being discussed by his audience.
TAB-FULL:v18p206/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {ولما ورد ماء مدين} [القصص: 23] قال علي بن موسى: قال: مثل ماء جوبكم هذا

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r1.claim: تذودان means the women were holding back their sheep, returning an animal that strayed; Arabic uses ذاد for restraining livestock.

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r2.claim: Some Kufan grammarians restrict ذاد to livestock and reject its use for restraining people; al-Ṭabarī counters that Arabic and Prophetic usage apply it to people too.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r2.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إني لبعقر حوضي أذود الناس عنه بعصاي»

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says he would hold people back at his basin with his staff, showing ذود can take people as its object.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إني لبعقر حوضي أذود الناس عنه بعصاي»

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r4.speaker: سويد بن كراع
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r4.claim: Suwayd ibn Kuraʿ’s verse uses أذود for keeping a herd of wild animals away, supporting the usage.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r4.anchor: ومن الذود قول سويد بن كراع: [البحر الطويل] أبيت على باب القوافي كأنما … أذود بها سربا من الوحش نزعا

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r5.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r5.claim: The other poet uses تذود for wielding a staff against people, also attesting human objects for the verb.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r5.anchor: وقول الآخر: [البحر الوافر] وقد سلبت عصاك بنو تميم … فما تدري بأي عصا تذود

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the women’s action as holding back their sheep.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {تذودان} [القصص: 23] يقول: تحبسان

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports from Ibn Abbas that the two women were holding the sheep back.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r7.anchor: سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، " {ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان} [القصص: 23]

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the women were holding back their sheep.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r8.anchor: عن السدي، " {ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان} [القصص: 23] يقول: تحبسان غنمهما

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r9.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r9.claim: Abu Malik says they held their sheep away from the water until the other people finished and the well was clear for them.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r9.anchor: عن أبي مالك، قوله: " {امرأتين تذودان} [القصص: 23] قال: تحبسان غنمهما عن الناس حتى يفرغوا

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r10.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r10.claim: Ibn Ishaq says they kept their sheep away from the water while the other people were there.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r10.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {ووجد من دونهم امرأتين} [القصص: 23] يعني دون القوم تذودان غنمهما عن الماء

TAB-FULL:v18p207/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r11.claim: Another reported interpretation is that the women kept people away from their sheep.
TAB-FULL:v18p207/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: تذودان الناس عن غنمهما.

TAB-FULL:v18p210/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r1.claim: Qatada says the women kept their sheep back and drove people away from them.
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان} [القصص: 23] قال: أي حابستين شاءهما

TAB-FULL:v18p210/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r2.speaker: أصحاب معمر
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r2.claim: Maʿmar’s associates gloss تذودان as driving people away from the women’s sheep.
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن أصحابه، {تذودان} [القصص: 23] قال: تذودان الناس عن غنمهما

TAB-FULL:v18p210/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p210/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the women held their sheep back until the other herders finished: their answer explains why they delayed watering, not why they guarded sheep from people.

TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r1.claim: ما خطبكما asks what their situation or affair was; Moses wondered why they held their animals apart instead of watering with the others.
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r1.anchor: ما شأنكما وأمركما تذودان ماشيتكما عن الناس، هلا تسقونها مع مواشي الناس

TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r2.claim: In Arabic, ما خطبك means “what is your affair or condition?”
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r2.anchor: ما خطبك: بمعنى ما أمرك وحالك

TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r3.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r3.claim: The rajaz poet’s line uses خطبه in the sense of one’s affair.
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r3.anchor: كما قال الراجز: [البحر الرجز] يا عجبا ما خطبه وخطبي

TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses asked why the women stood apart and did not water alongside the people.
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال لهما: " {ما خطبكما} [القصص: 23] معتزلتين لا تسقيان مع الناس؟

TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses felt pity and concern for their weakness as the crowd dominated the water, so he asked what their situation was.
TAB-FULL:v18p210#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " وجد لهما رحمة، ودخلته فيهما خشية، لما رأى من ضعفهما، وغلبة الناس على الماء دونهما

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r1.claim: The women wait until the shepherds leave with their flocks because they cannot water alongside them; they use whatever water remains in the trough.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما قال موسى للمرأتين: ما خطبكما؟ قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the women cannot water until the people water, so they follow the leftover water.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما قال موسى للمرأتين: ما خطبكما؟ قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the women wait to water from what remains in the shepherds’ troughs.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: " {حتى يصدر الرعاء} [القصص: 23] قال: تنتظر أن تسقيان من فضول ما في الحياض

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the women could not jostle with men, and their elderly father could not water; they wait until others finish, then water and leave.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء} [القصص: 23] امرأتان لا نستطيع أن نزاحم الرجال

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains al-riʿāʾ as a plural of rāʿī and lists riʿāʾ, ruʿāt, and riʿyān as plural forms.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: " {حتى يصدر الرعاء} [القصص: 23] قال: تنتظر أن تسقيان من فضول ما في الحياض

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r6.speaker: عامة قراء الحجاز سوى أبي جعفر وعامة قراء العراق سوى أبي عمرو
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r6.claim: Most readers in the Hijaz except Abū Jaʿfar and in Iraq except Abū ʿAmr read yuṣdir with ḍamma on yāʾ, meaning the shepherds send their flocks away.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r6.anchor: فقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الحجاز سوى أبي جعفر القارئ وعامة قراء العراق سوى أبي عمرو

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAmr read yaṣduru with fatḥa on yāʾ, meaning the shepherds depart from the watering place.
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r7.anchor: وقرأ ذلك أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو بفتح الياء من يصدر الرعاء عن الحوض

TAB-FULL:v18p211/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p211/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī judges the two readings close in meaning and says either is correct because recognized readers used each.

SULAMI:v2p102#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r1.claim: The one who arrives seeks escape from the burden of service, while the one who leads seeks encounter and attainment.
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : الوارد يطلب المفالته لثقل الخدمة والقاد يطلب اللقاء

SULAMI:v2p102#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r2.claim: Moses came outwardly to Midian’s water and inwardly to the possessor of intimacy’s waters and the gardens of gnosis; meeting the elect and drinking there gave him steadfastness in intimate address.
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : ورد في الظاهر ماء مدين وورد في الحقيقة على مالك مياه الأنس

SULAMI:v2p102#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r3.claim: Moses was turned toward God and separated from all else; after hardship he rested in God’s shade, then voiced his need for the good God sent him (28:24).
SULAMI:v2p102#4/r3.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا بكر بن طاهر يقول : وقد سئل عن قوله

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.claim: This episode recounts Moses’ flight from Egypt after killing the Egyptian, his arrival in Midian, and his marriage there to an unnamed elder’s daughter.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.anchor: يذكر فيه خروجه من مصر إلى مدين عقيب قتله القبطي خوفا من فرعون

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r9.claim: ذود means to restrain or prevent; the women held their sheep back from the water or from mingling with the men’s flocks.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r9.anchor: الذود الحبس والمنع، والمراد بقوله { تذودان } أنهما يحبسان أغنامهما

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r10.claim: يسقون refers to watering livestock, and الرعاء is the plural of راعٍ, a shepherd.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r10.anchor: جمع الراعي وهو الذي يرعى الغنم

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r11.claim: At the well Moses saw people watering their flocks and two women nearby keeping their sheep back; he asked what was wrong because no man was with them.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r11.anchor: وجد على الماء جماعة من الناس يسقون أغنامهم ووجد بالقرب منهم مما يليه امرأتين تحبسان أغنامهما

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r12.claim: The women said they waited until the shepherds departed, since their elderly father could not undertake the watering and they had taken it on themselves.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r12.anchor: قالتا لا نسقي غنمنا أي عادتنا ذلك حتى يصدر الراعون

TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.claim: A report from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq recounts Moses’ exhausting flight to Midian, where he drew water for two young women unable to jostle with the men; they brought him to their father.
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث طويل وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى

FARRA:v2p304/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p304/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p304/r2.claim: تذودان means holding their sheep back; ذود is restraining livestock that stray, while ذدت الرجل is not valid for restraining a man.
FARRA:v2p304/r2.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تقول ذدت الرجل: حبسته. وإنما كان الذياد حبسا للغنم

FARRA:v2p304/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p304/r3.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v2p304/r3.claim: Abdullah’s reading has حابستان, describing the women as holding their flock back.
FARRA:v2p304/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله (ودونهم امرأتان حابستان) فسألهما عن حبسهما

FARRA:v2p304/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p304/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p304/r4.claim: The women said they could not water their flock until the men left; Moses obtained a bucket, which forty or so normally carried, drew water alone, and watered their sheep.
FARRA:v2p304/r4.anchor: قالتا: لا نقوى على السقي مع الناس حتى يصدروا. فأتى أهل الماء فاستوهبهم دلوا فقالوا: استق إن قويت

THALABI:v7p243#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243#2/r1.claim: Madyan's water was a well, where people watered their livestock; the two women stood apart restraining their sheep from straying.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r1.anchor: ولما ورد ماء مدين وهو بئر كانت لهم وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون مواشيهم

THALABI:v7p243#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p243#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the women kept their sheep from mixing with other people's flocks; the mention of sheep is omitted for brevity.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: تكفان [أغنامهما] عن أن تختلط بأغنام الناس

THALABI:v7p243#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p243#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the women were keeping the people away from their sheep.

THALABI:v7p243#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r4.speaker: أبو مالك وابن إسحاق
THALABI:v7p243#2/r4.claim: Abu Malik and Ibn Ishaq say they kept their flock back until the shepherds had left the water, then watered it because they were weak; the author prefers this as it best fits what follows.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r4.anchor: أبو مالك وابن إسحاق: تحبسان غنمهما عن الماء حتى يصدر عنه مواشي الناس

THALABI:v7p243#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243#2/r5.claim: Khatb means their situation or business: why were they not watering their livestock with the others?
THALABI:v7p243#2/r5.anchor: ما خطبكما ما شأنكما لا تسقيان مواشيكما مع الناس

THALABI:v7p243#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن عامر وابن جعفر وأيوب بن المتوكل
THALABI:v7p243#2/r6.claim: These readers open the yāʾ and damma the dāl, making the shepherds the subject: the women wait until the shepherds return from the water.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن عامر وابن جعفر وأيوب بن المتوكل: بفتح الياء وضم الدال

THALABI:v7p243#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r7.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v7p243#2/r7.claim: The other readers damma the yāʾ and kasra the dāl, meaning the shepherds drive their livestock away from the water.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بضم الياء وكسر الدال أي حتى يصرفوا مواشيهم عن الماء

THALABI:v7p243#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243#2/r8.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿi, on the pattern of tujjar from tājir; the women cannot compete with the men and water only after the shepherds leave the flock's remainder in the trough.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r8.anchor: والرعاء: جمع راع مثل تاجر وتجار، ومعنى الآية لا نسقي مواشينا

THALABI:v7p243#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243#2/r9.claim: Their father is too old to water his livestock himself.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r9.anchor: وأبونا شيخ كبير لا يقدر أن يسقي مواشيه

THALABI:v7p243#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن
THALABI:v7p243#2/r10.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Hasan identify their father as the prophet Shuʿayb, named Shuʿayb ibn Buwayb ibn Midyan ibn Abraham.

THALABI:v7p243#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243#2/r11.speaker: وهب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
THALABI:v7p243#2/r11.claim: Wahb, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Abu ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allah identify the father as Buthrun, Shuʿayb's nephew; Shuʿayb had died blind and was buried between the Maqam and Zamzam.
THALABI:v7p243#2/r11.anchor: قال وهب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو عبيدة بن عبد الله: هو بثرون ابن أخي شعيب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r1.claim: Umma here means a group of people.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r1.anchor: {وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون} أي جماعة (1) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r2.claim: Tadhūdān means the two women were keeping their sheep back; the object “sheep” is omitted for concision.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r2.anchor: {ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان} أي تكفان غنمهما.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r3.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ's commentary says one woman held the sheep back for the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r3.anchor: وفي تفسير أبي صالح: "تحبس إحداهما الغنم على الأخرى". (2)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r4.claim: Mā khaṭbukumā means “what is your affair or situation?”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r4.anchor: قال ما خطبكما} أي ما أمركما؟ وما شأنكما؟

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r5.claim: The form yaṣduru al-riʿāʾ means the shepherds return from the water.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r6.speaker: قارئ غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r6.claim: A reading with the shepherds as transitive agents means that they drive their sheep away from the water.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ: {يصدر الرعاء} ؛ أراد: يرد الرعاء أغنامهم عن الماء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r1.claim: The umma is a group of people, namely shepherds watering their livestock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون} جماعة من الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r2.claim: Most commentators identify the two women as the daughters of Shuʿayb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r2.anchor: أي: من سوى الأمة {امرأتين} وهما: ابنتا شعيب، في قول أكثر المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r3.claim: The root dh-w-d means to restrain or drive away; tadhūdāni means they push back and hold something off.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r3.anchor: ومعنى الذود في اللغة: الكف والطرد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r4.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل وسعيد بن جبير والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r4.claim: Most commentators say the women held their sheep back; Muqātil says they waited to water after the shepherds, while al-Suddī says they kept the sheep aside until the others cleared the well.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r4.anchor: هذا قول أكثر المفسرين؛ الكلبي ومقاتل وسعيد بن جبير والسدي، وغيرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r5.claim: Muqātil says they held the sheep so they could water from what the other shepherds left.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: حابستين الغنم، لتسقيا الغنم فضل الرعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r6.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says they kept their sheep away until the others finished and left the well for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: تحبسان غنمهما عن الناس حتى يفرغوا، ويخلوا لهم البئر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r7.claim: The object sheep is omitted for brevity: they were restraining their sheep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسلم: أي تكفان غنمهما، وحذف الغنم اختصارا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r8.claim: Since the verse does not name what they kept the sheep from, most exegetes take it as the water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r8.anchor: ولم يذكر في الآية عن أي شيء تدفعان الغنم، فذهب أكثر أهل التفسير إلى أنهما كانتا تدفعانها عن الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r9.claim: Abū Isḥāq favors keeping the sheep from the well because the people watering were stronger than the women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r9.anchor: واختاره أبو إسحاق؛ قال: {تذودان} غنمهما عن أن تقرب موضع الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r10.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they kept their sheep from mixing with other people's flocks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: تكفان الغنم عن أن تختلط بأغنام الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r11.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r11.claim: Qatāda says they were keeping people away from their sheep.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says they restrained their sheep from straying; he rejects saying dhudtu al-rajul for restraining a person, explaining that driving a sheep back amounts to holding it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: تحبسانها عن أن تشذ وتذهب، قال: ولا يجوز أن يقال: ذدت الرجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r13.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r13.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses the question as asking why the women do not water their animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r13.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: ما شأنكما لا تسقيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r14.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains khatb as their business or purpose in keeping the flock from water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r14.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي ما أمركما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r15.claim: The first explanation fits: if they were not holding the sheep from water during watering time, Moses would not have asked what was wrong; their reply explains why they waited.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r15.anchor: والقول هو الأول؛ لقوله: {قال ما خطبكما}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r16.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p368/r16.claim: A reading from ṣadara, the opposite of warada, means the shepherds return from watering.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r1.claim: On another reading, the women wait until the shepherds send their animals away from the watering place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ: {يصدر} أراد حين يصدروا مواشيهم من وردهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the omitted object as so they clear the place for us.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فيخلوا لنا الموضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r3.claim: Riʿāʾ is a plural of rāʿ, like tājir/tujjār and ṣāḥib/ṣaḥāb; it also has the plural rāʿāh, like al-bukāh, al-ghuzāh, and al-duʿāh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r3.anchor: {الرعاء}: جمع راع، كما يقال: تاجر وتجار، وصاحب وصحاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r4.claim: The women wait until the shepherds return with their flocks from water to pasture, then water from what remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: {قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء} بالغنم راجعة من الماء إلى الرعي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r5.claim: They cannot jostle with men, and their elderly father cannot water the livestock, so they wait until the men finish and then water and leave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r5.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: {قالتا} نحن امرأتان لا نستطيع أن نزاحم الرجال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r6.claim: Muqātil says their father was too old to water the sheep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: لا يستطيع أن يسقي الغنم من الكبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r7.claim: Mentioning their father explains that he cannot go out and water, so the women have to draw water themselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r7.anchor: أي: لا يمكنه أن يرد ويسقي، فلذلك احتجنا ونحن نساء أن نستقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says their old father had no helper other than them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قالتا: {وأبونا شيخ كبير} وليس له عون يعينه غير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r9.claim: Moses asked the people at the well for a bucket; though forty men usually lifted it, he drew it alone, poured it into a trough, prayed for blessing, and watered the women's flock until it was full.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r9.anchor: وكان يجتمع على الدلو أربعون رجلا حتى يخرجوه من البئر، فأخذ موسى الدلو فاستقى به وحده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r10.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r10.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses took their bucket and used his strength to move the other waterers away, then watered for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r10.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق (¬4): أخذ موسى دلوهما ثم تقدم إلى السقاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r11.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r11.claim: Muqātil says Moses lifted the stone covering the well alone, drew one bucket, poured it into the trough, prayed for blessing, and watered the flock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p371/r11.anchor: وقال مقاتل: قال لهما موسى: أين الماء؟ فانطلقتا به إلى الماء، فإذا هو بحجر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r3.claim: The water of Midian was their well, where a group of people watered their livestock.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r3.anchor: وهو بئر لهم { وجد عليه أمة } جماعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r4.claim: The two women held their sheep back from the water until the shepherds finished, since they could not draw water while competing with the men; their father was too old to do it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r4.anchor: لأنا لا نطيق أن نستقي وأن نزاحم الرجال، فإذا صدروا سقينا من فضل مواشيهم { وأبونا شيخ كبير } لا يمكنه أن يرد وأن يستقي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p586/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p586/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p586/r1.claim: Al-Suddi explains that their father was advanced in age.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p586/r1.anchor: قال السدي، يعني: كبيرا في السن.

MAJAZ:v2p102/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p102/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p102/r1.claim: Mā khaṭbukumā asks what your affair, condition, or situation is; the poem ‘what is his affair and mine?’ witnesses khaṭb.
MAJAZ:v2p102/r1.anchor: قال ما خطبكما» (23) أي ما أمركما وحالكما وشأنكما، قال: يا عجبا ما خطبه وخطبى

ELMALILI:28:23-28/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r1.claim: Wurud is going to water, sudur is returning from it, and isdar is taking the animals away from the water.
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r1.anchor: “Vürûd” suya gitmek, “sudûr” sudan dönmek olduğu gibi, “ısdâr” da hayvanları sudan çekip götürmektir.

ELMALILI:28:23-28/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r2.claim: Ri'a is the plural of ra'i, meaning shepherds.

ELMALILI:28:23-28/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r3.claim: Tadhudani comes from dhawdh, to prevent or repel; the women hold their animals back while the others water theirs.
ELMALILI:28:23-28/r3.anchor: ذود Zevd: men‘ü def‘etmek, yani diğerleri sularken bu ikisi hayvanlarını sakındırıp duruyorlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.claim: Because Midian's people were Arab and close to the Israelites in ethnicity and language, it is historically plausible that they helped Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.anchor: Buranın halkı Arap asıllı olduğu için Hz. Mûsâ’nın soyundan olan İbrânîler’e hem ırk hem de dil bakımından yakındılar, dolayısıyla ona yardım etmiş olmaları tarihen mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r3.speaker: tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r3.claim: Exegetical accounts identify the two women at the well as daughters of the prophet Shuʿayb, sent to Midian.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r3.anchor: Tefsirlerde anlatıldığına göre Hz. Mûsâ’nın Medyen suyu başında gördüğü iki kadın Medyen halkına peygamber olarak gönderilmiş olan Şuayb aleyhisselâmın kızları olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r4.speaker: rivayetler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r4.claim: Other reports say the women were daughters of Shuʿayb's nephew or of a righteous man from Midian.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r4.anchor: Bunların Şuayb’ın kardeşi oğlunun veya Medyen halkından sâlih birinin kızları olduğuna dair rivayetler de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r5.speaker: tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r5.claim: The women could water their animals only after the people had watered theirs and left the well.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r5.anchor: ancak halk hayvanlarını sulayıp kuyunun başından ayrıldıktan sonra hayvanlarını sulayabiliyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r6.claim: When Moses asked about their situation, the women indirectly sought help by saying they were weak and their father was elderly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r6.anchor: Kızlar, Mûsâ’nın sorusu üzerine kendilerinin güçsüz, babalarının da ihtiyar olduğunu söyleyerek dolaylı bir şekilde yardım istemişlerdir

BURHAN:v3p162/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p162/r7.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p162/r7.claim: Al-Sakkākī counts five omitted objects in the account of Moses at Midian, on the reading with kasra on the dāl in yuṣdir.
BURHAN:v3p162/r7.anchor: وجعل منه السكاكي قوله تعالى ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون

BURHAN:v3p162/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p162/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p162/r8.claim: The author judges those five cases more likely to belong to the second category of object omission.
BURHAN:v3p162/r8.anchor: والأقرب أنه من الضرب الثاني كما سنبينه فيه إن شاء الله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p383/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p383/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p383/r1.claim: لما introduces a temporal condition; its answer may be an explicit nominal clause with fa, a negated clause, or an إذا-fajʾiyya clause.
BURHAN:v4p383/r1.anchor: واما جوابها فقد يجئ ظاهرا كما ذكرنا قد يكون جملة اسمية مقرونة بالفاء

BURHAN:v4p383/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p383/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p383/r2.claim: A present-tense verb may answer لما while conveying past meaning, as in Abraham's disputing after the fear left him.

ITQAN:v2p573/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p573/r1.speaker: السكاكي
ITQAN:v2p573/r1.claim: Al-Sakkaki calls it the wise style when an answer departs from the question’s apparent demand to show what should have been asked; answers may also be broader or narrower as circumstances require.
ITQAN:v2p573/r1.anchor: وقد يعدل في الجواب عما يقتضيه السؤال تنبيها على أنه كان من حق السؤال أن يكون كذلك ويسميه السكاكي الأسلوب الحكيم

ITQAN:v2p573/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p573/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p573/r2.claim: The author notes that an answer may be broader than a question when needed, or narrower when circumstances call for it.
ITQAN:v2p573/r2.anchor: وقد يجيء الجواب أعم من السؤال للحاجة إليه في السؤال وقد يجيء أنقص لاقتضاء الحال ذلك

NAHHAS:v3p234/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p234/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses تذودان as holding back; the verb can also mean leading, since leading restrains an animal toward the leader’s intended direction.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r1.anchor: فقد ذكرنا قول ابن عباس إن معنى تذودان تحبسان وذلك معروف في اللغة يقال ذاده يذوده إذا حبسه وإذا قاده

NAHHAS:v3p234/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p234/r2.claim: The women kept their flock from the water because they were unable to draw water and other flocks drove theirs away.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r2.anchor: وإنما كانتا تحبسان غنمهما لأنهما لا طاقة لهما بالسقي وكانت غنمهما تطرد عن الماء

NAHHAS:v3p234/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p234/r3.claim: ما خطبكما is a subject-predicate construction.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r3.anchor: قال ما خطبكما مبتدأ وخبره قال أبو إسحاق

NAHHAS:v3p234/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p234/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses the question as asking why they are keeping their sheep from the water.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق والمعنى ما تريدان بذود غنمكما عن الماء

NAHHAS:v3p234/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p234/r5.claim: لا نسقي means the women are unable to water their flock; they wait until the shepherds have dealt with theirs.

NAHHAS:v3p234/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r6.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأهل الحرمين
NAHHAS:v3p234/r6.claim: The Kufans and the two sanctuary regions except Abū Jaʿfar read causative يصدر: the herders send their animals away from the water; Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAmr read intransitive يصدر, “the herders depart.” Both make sense, but the causative better fits the context. Abū Ḥātim says the first means they send out their flocks, not that the herders leave.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r6.anchor: قراءة أهل الكوفة وأهل الحرمين إلا أبا جعفر فإنه قرأ

NAHHAS:v3p234/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r7.speaker: يعقوب
NAHHAS:v3p234/r7.claim: رعاء is a plural of راع like صحاب from صاحب; Yaʿqūb also reports ruʿāʾ with ḍamma, which Abū Ḥātim rejects, though al-Naḥḥās says it is possible like غزاء and غزا from غاز.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r7.anchor: و الرعاء جمع راع كما تقول صاحب وصحاب قال يعقوب وذكر لي

NAHHAS:v3p234/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p234/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p234/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the father’s old age explains why he could not come water the flock, forcing the two women to go out.
NAHHAS:v3p234/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الفائدة في وأبونا شيخ أنه لا يمكنه أن يحضر فيسقي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r1.claim: The narrative omits the objects of four actions: the people water their livestock, the women drive away their own flock, they say they will not water it, and Moses waters it for them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r1.anchor: ففيها حذف مفعول في أربعة مواضع إذ المعنى : وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون أغنامهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r2.claim: Leaving the objects unspoken keeps attention on the occurrence and agents of watering and driving away; the particular animals are irrelevant and naming them could misleadingly make the conduct itself seem objectionable only for sheep.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r2.anchor: وما ذاك إلا أن الغرض في أن يعلم أنه كان من الناس في تلك الحال سقي ، ومن المرأتين ذود

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r3.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r3.claim: In the cited verse, omitting the object makes wasting and healing seem inherent in distance and closeness, a nuance impossible to preserve if the object is stated.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p131/r3.anchor: قول البحتري ، + الطويل + : ( إذا بعدت أبلت وإن قربت شفت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r1.claim: Ali b. Ubayd Allah says the basic sense of wurūd is setting out to seek, especially in seeking water.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الأصل في الورود : أنه السعي للطلب . وهو الأعم الأظهر في طلب الماء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r2.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r2.claim: He says returning from the water is called ṣadr.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الأصل في الورود : أنه السعي للطلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r3.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r3.claim: He says reaching a destination is called wurūd because reaching it is the aim of setting out.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r3.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الأصل في الورود : أنه السعي للطلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r4.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r4.claim: He says the place sought for water is also called wurūd.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r4.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الأصل في الورود : أنه السعي للطلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r5.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r5.claim: A thirsty arrival is called ward because thirst prompts the journey; the term is also used figuratively.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r5.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الأصل في الورود : أنه السعي للطلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r6.claim: One Qur'anic sense is entering, as in the verses about entering the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الورد في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r7.claim: A second sense is being present at the Fire, which the source glosses as attending it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الورد في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r8.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r8.claim: Some scholars subsume the sense of being present under the preceding sense of entering.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r8.anchor: وقد ألحقه قوم بالقسم الذي قبله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r9.claim: A third sense is reaching or arriving; this is the sense in the verse about Moses reaching Midian's water.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الورد في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r10.claim: A fourth sense is seeking, as in the water seeker sent by a caravan.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الورد في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r11.claim: A fifth sense is thirst: the condemned are driven to Hell thirsty.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r11.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الورد في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن اليزيدي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r12.claim: Al-Yazidi relates wardan, “thirsty,” to the verb meaning “I came to water.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p609/r12.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن اليزيدي : وردا من وردت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r8.claim: The group at the watering place was a company of people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r8.anchor: {ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس} [القصص: 23] جماعة من الناس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r9.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r9.claim: Qatāda says the two women were keeping people away from their sheep.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r9.anchor: {يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان} [القصص: 23] قال قتادة: تذودان الناس عن شائهما.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r10.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r10.claim: A reading cited in Qatāda’s interpretation adds that the women were keeping people away from their sheep.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r10.anchor: وفي بعض الحروف: تذودان الناس عن شائهما: أي: حابستين شاءهما تذودان الناس عنها، في تفسير قتادة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r11.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r11.claim: Another explanation is that the women kept their flock from mixing with other people’s flocks.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم يمنعان غنمهما أن تختلط بأغنام الناس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r12.claim: Moses’ question means “What is your situation?”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r12.anchor: قال لهما موسى: {ما خطبكما} [القصص: 23] : ما أمركما؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r13.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r13.claim: In Qatāda’s gloss, as cited in al-Ḥasan’s interpretation, the women waited until the people watered their flocks and then collected what remained.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r13.anchor: {قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء} [القصص: 23] قال قتادة: أي: حتى يسقي الناس ثم نتتبع فضالتهم في تفسير الحسن.

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r8.claim: When Moses arrived in Midian at midday, its pastoral people were drawing water from a well, pouring it into troughs, and watering their sheep.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r8.anchor: لما وافى مدين شعيب كان وقت الهاجرة ، وكانت لهم بئر يستقون منها ، فيصبون الماء في الحياض

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r9.speaker: القصة
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r9.claim: The story says the prophet Shuʿayb repeatedly wept until he lost his sight; when God restored it and asked why, he said he wept from longing for God, not fear of Hell or desire for Paradise.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r9.anchor: ففي القصة أنه بكى فذهب بصره ، ثم رد الله عليه بصره فبكى ، فرد الله بصره

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r10.speaker: القصة
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r10.claim: The story says God promised Shuʿayb Paradise or safety from Hell and, because he wept from longing, honored him by placing Moses in his service for ten years.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r10.anchor: لخوف النار فقد أمنتك ، وإن كان

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r11.claim: Shuʿayb had sheep but no hired shepherd; his two daughters tended them, unable to draw water, and waited until the shepherds finished before using any water left in the trough.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r11.anchor: وكانت لشعيب أغنام ، ولم يكن لديه أجير ، فكانت بنتاه تسوقان الغنم مكان الرعاة

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r12.claim: Moses saw the daughters keeping their flock from the water, felt pity, asked their situation, watered their sheep when the shepherds left, and then withdrew to the shade of a wall.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r12.anchor: فلما وافى موسى ذلك اليوم وشاهد ذلك ورآهما يمنعان غنمهما عن الماء رق قلبه لهما

BURHAN:v1p108/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p108/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p108/r13.claim: Warada usually means to enter; when Moses came to the water of Midian, it means he approached it without entering.
BURHAN:v1p108/r13.anchor: الورود فى القرآن الدخول إلا فى القصص

BURHAN:v3p176/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p176/r2.claim: In the Midian episode, objects are omitted from watering and fending verbs: the passage foregrounds the actions and encounter, while whether the animals were sheep, camels, or something else is beside its point.
BURHAN:v3p176/r2.anchor: حذف منها المفعول خمس مرات لأنه غير مراد

BURHAN:v3p176/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p176/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the objects are omitted because the action, not the watered animals, is the point; Moses helped the women because they were fending while others watered, not because their animals were a particular kind.
BURHAN:v3p176/r3.anchor: موافقة للزمخشري فإنه قال ترك المفعول لأن الغرض هو الفعل لا المفعول

BURHAN:v3p176/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r4.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p176/r4.claim: Al-Sakkaki classifies these omitted objects as deletion for concision even though the objects remain intended.
BURHAN:v3p176/r4.anchor: وجعله السكاكي من الضرب الأول أعني مما حذف فيه للاختصار مع الإرادة

BURHAN:v3p176/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r5.speaker: الجزري
BURHAN:v3p176/r5.claim: Al-Jazari prefers al-Sakkaki: the sheep matter because their weakness, combined with the women’s weakness, makes their need more deserving of compassion and help.
BURHAN:v3p176/r5.anchor: فإن الغنم ليست ساقطة عن الاعتبار بالأصالة فإن فيها ضعفا

BURHAN:v3p176/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p176/r6.claim: Zarkashi says al-Zamakhshari’s analysis is nearer, since the excerpt’s focus is the act of tending or watering rather than the object.

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

BURHAN:v1p288/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p288/r2.claim: Wa-ṭafiqa is glossed as intending or setting out, from Roman usage.

ITQAN:v2p418/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r15.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r15.claim: Wurūd usually means entering, but Moses' coming to the well of Midian means approaching it, not entering it.
ITQAN:v2p418/r15.anchor: وكل ورود فيه دخول إلا ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين ﴾ يعني هجم عليه ولم يدخله

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r4.claim: Moses helps the two women because they are keeping the flock back while their people water theirs; the point is their act of watering, not the particular animals watered.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r4.anchor: ألا ترى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام رحمهما إذ كانتا على صفة الذياد وقومهما على السقي

ITQAN:v4p391/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r4.claim: The two women tending the flock are Liya and Safuriya; one is the woman Moses married.
ITQAN:v4p391/r4.anchor: هما ليا وصفوريا وهي التي نكحها وأبوهما شعيب

ITQAN:v4p391/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r5.claim: Their father is identified as Shuʿayb.
ITQAN:v4p391/r5.anchor: وأبوهما شعيب وقيل يثرون ابن أخي شعيب

ITQAN:v4p391/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r6.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p391/r6.claim: An alternative says their father is Yathrun, Shuʿayb's nephew.

DAMGHANI:v1p431/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r7.claim: The two women at the well are the daughters of Shuʿayb.
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r7.anchor: العاشر : المراتان ابنتا شعيب . قوله تعالى فى سورة القصص

DAMGHANI:v1p431/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r8.claim: An alternative identification says the two women were daughters of Shuʿayb's brother's son Yathrun.

DAMGHANI:v1p483/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r12.claim: Warada can mean reaching a place, as Moses reached the water of Midian.
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r12.anchor: الثاني الورود البلوغ قوله تعالى في سورة القصص ولما ورد ماء مدين أي بلغ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r10.speaker: author
